description: Required for VirtIO-MMIO transport — Firecracker's default device transport. All VirtIO devices (block, net, vsock, balloon, entropy) need this on aarch64 always; on x86_64 either this or PCI VirtIO.
Guest VirtIO block driver. Required to mount any /dev/vd* disk attached via PUT /drives.
Guest VirtIO network driver. Required for any network interface attached via PUT /network-interfaces.
Guest vsock driver. Required for any host↔guest vsock comms via PUT /vsock.
Guest balloon device driver. Required for memory reclaim via PATCH /balloon. Pairs with CONFIG_MEMORY_BALLOON.
Guest VirtIO entropy/RNG driver. Required for the entropy device attached via PUT /entropy. Without it, guest may stall at boot waiting for entropy.
Guest uses CPU RNG instructions (RDRAND etc.) to initialize the kernel RNG. Available kernel ≥5.10. Reduces boot-time entropy starvation even without virtio-rng.

x86_64. Required for the ACPI boot path. Supersedes the legacy MPTable/cmdline-virtio mechanism. CONFIG_PCI must also be enabled (ACPI initialization relies on it even when no PCI devices are exposed).
x86_64. Required for ACPI boot AND for --enable-pci VirtIO transport. Counter-intuitive: needed even when no PCI devices exist (ACPI init dependency).
Guest VirtIO over PCI driver. Required only when Firecracker is started with --enable-pci.
x86_64. Enables KVM paravirt features in the guest including CONFIG_KVM_CLOCK (kvm-clock timekeeping). Effectively required for any modern x86_64 guest.

x86_64 LEGACY. Enables MPTable parsing — the pre-ACPI device-enumeration mechanism. Disabling it (CONFIG_X86_MPPARSE=n) avoids the double-init warnings when the guest also has CONFIG_ACPI=y. Recommended off for ACPI-only guests.
x86_64 LEGACY. Enables device enumeration via virtio_mmio.device= kernel cmdline params. Disable when using ACPI to avoid double-init.
Disables loadable kernel module support. Smaller attack surface; faster boot. Default in Firecracker's boot_args.
Disables 8250 UART probing. Combined with `console=ttyS0` being absent from defaults, makes serial-console output a deliberate opt-in for debugging.

Skips probing the i8042 keyboard controller for an auxiliary mouse, multiplexing, and state control. Saves boot time. Firecracker emulates i8042 only enough to detect the reset-line write that terminates the process.
Disables forced software bounce-buffer (SWIOTLB) usage. Faster I/O when not needed for high memory or DMA constraints.
x86_64 only. Switch all VirtIO devices to PCI transport instead of MMIO. Higher throughput + lower latency. Requires PCI-enabled guest kernel and removing pci=off from boot_args.
